page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and features a 45 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highcpu-4 in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused workloads, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1125.48 and a multi-core score of 2941.66, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show limited throughput, with a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.99 GB/sec and a passmark CPU encryption score of 1338.88. Memory performance is constrained, as evidenced by a passmark memory score of 987.38 and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 25.58 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its highly restricted memory capacity of 1.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. Given the weak multi-core performance and low memory bandwidth, this instance is best suited for lightweight compute-bound tasks, basic software compilation, or low-traffic static web serving. It is not recommended for database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or memory-heavy data processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance from the n1 family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with hyperthreading, a 45 MB L3 cache, and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate weak to poor processing capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, reaching 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Due to these resource limitations and lower-tier benchmark results, the n1-highcpu-4 is best utilized for lightweight, CPU-focused workloads such as basic software compilation, minor text processing, and low-throughput static web serving, rather than memory-intensive or high-performance database applications.
